J1.evidence: Arabic Sarf: «إمّا أن يكون جمعا لتابع مثل خدم وخادم.. فهو اسم فاعل من تبع الثلاثيّ وزنه فاعل» - فهو = 'so it is'. English: 'in which case [the singular] is the active participle' inserts '[the singular]' in bare brackets, an interpretive addition that also silently adjusts the source; it is not inside «[Translator's note: …]». Fix: 'so it is an active participle...' plus a translator note (as the Turkish does).

J2.evidence: Sarf: «(تبعا) ، إمّا أن يكون جمعا لتابع مثل خدم وخادم.. فهو اسم فاعل من تبع الثلاثيّ وزنه فاعل». EN 'in which case [the singular] is the active participle' inserts '[the singular]', which is not in the Arabic (only فهو) and is not inside a [Translator's note: ...]; unmarked interpretive addition. TR handles the same issue with a Mütercim notu. Fix: render فهو literally and move the interpretation into a Translator's note.
